title: Nonuniform QCPH Collapse Implies QCPH Collapse
abstract: Despite the importance of the non-uniform Polynomial-Time Hierarchy (PH/poly) in classical complexity understanding the collapse conditions of the Polynomial-Time Hierarchy (PH), a quantum equivalent of PH/poly has yet to be studied in the literature. We introduce the non-uniform computational Quantum Polynomial-Time Hierarchy (QCPH/mpoly), the quantum equivalent of PH/poly, and show that it collapses if and only if QCPH, the quantum equivalent of PH introduced by Gharibian et al. (comput. complex. 2022), also collapses. We also show that QCPH collapses if coQCMA is contained in QCMA/mpoly. These results are analogous to those of Yap (TCS 1983) commonly used to invoke the collapse of PH in classical complexity. QCPH/mpoly is analogous to QCPH with non-uniform quantum verifier circuits.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the collapse conditions for the Quantum Polynomial-Time Hierarchy ($	ext{QCPH}$). It introduces the non-uniform quantum analogue ($	ext{QCPH/mpoly}$) and proves that its collapse is equivalent to the collapse of the standard $	ext{QCPH}$. The work employs advanced techniques from quantum complexity theory to draw deep connections between different levels of the quantum hierarchy.
main_problem: The paper aims to study the collapse conditions of the Quantum Polynomial-Time Hierarchy ($	ext{QCPH}$) and its non-uniform variant ($	ext{QCPH/mpoly}$).
main_result: It establishes that the collapse of the non-uniform hierarchy ($	ext{QCPH/mpoly}$) is equivalent to the collapse of the standard quantum hierarchy ($	ext{QCPH}$), providing quantum analogues to classical complexity results.
method: The analysis uses advanced techniques from quantum complexity theory, involving the definition and comparison of quantum complexity classes ($	ext{QC}\Sigma_i, 	ext{QC}\Pi_i$) and the construction of complex advice functions ($	ext{a}'''$) to prove inclusions and equivalences.
model_or_system: The model is purely theoretical, dealing with computational complexity classes defined over quantum computation models, specifically the Quantum Polynomial-Time Hierarchy ($	ext{QCPH}$).
key_observables: The collapse of the hierarchies (e.g., $	ext{QCPH} = 	ext{QC}\Sigma_i = 	ext{QC}\Pi_i$).
important_parameters: The index $i$ of the hierarchy level, and the polynomial size constraints on advice functions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of polynomial advice functions and relies on established results regarding the structure of the quantum polynomial hierarchy.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the non-uniform quantum complexity class $	ext{QCPH/mpoly}$ and proves several theorems relating its collapse to the collapse of $	ext{QCPH}$ and its uniform counterparts ($	ext{QC}\Sigma_i/	ext{mpoly}$ and $	ext{QC}\Pi_i/	ext{mpoly}$), building upon analogous classical results.
why_interesting: Although highly abstract, understanding the computational limits of quantum algorithms (like the collapse of $	ext{QCPH}$) is fundamental to assessing the theoretical power and feasibility of quantum computation for physical simulations.
